summary: The New Gloucester Opportunity Farm tower is listed as gone; 1950-51 'New Gloucester' tower notes do not name the farm, and the Fryeburg move is unconfirmed.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists the site as gone and says the Fryeburg Fairgrounds tower came from it; the fair's profile describes a 2009 replica and does not mention a move.

staffing.status: attendant named in April and August 1950 newspaper notes; watchman appointed for the 1951 season

corrections.why: FFLA lists this site as 'Tower Gone'. The relocation to Fryeburg is FFLA's tag on a different entry, and the fair's profile does not confirm it.

corrections.current: None relocated (The lookout was moved to the Fryeburg Fairgrounds.)
corrections.proposed: No confirmed relocation. FFLA says the Fryeburg Fairgrounds tower came from here; the fair's profile describes a 2009 replica and does not confirm a move.
corrections.why: The record states the move as fact, but the only source for it is FFLA's relocated tag, which the fair's profile does not support.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA marks the New Gloucester site gone and the Fryeburg Fairgrounds tower as relocated from it. The fair's profile describes a 2009 replica built by the fair and does not mention New Gloucester. The story reports the site as gone and the move as unconfirmed.

sources.title: Meet Howard Hatch, Fryeburg Fair's Fire Tower

notes_for_editor: No build date, design or height was found for the New Gloucester tower. The 1950-51 notes say 'New Gloucester fire tower' and never name the farm, so the link to FFLA's Opportunity Farm entry is an inference. FFLA's coordinates for this site (43.95342, -70.29415) are the record's own. Fryeburg details are in the sibling record us-me-opportunity-farm-at-fryeburg-fairgrounds. The Conway Daily Sun replica article was not read (HTTP 429 in an earlier pass). Maine Memory and Facebook search hits were not used as sources.
